Hi all — thanks for the loop. Summary of what we can provide and redaction approach:

1) Deliverables we will produce:
   - Redacted adversary simulation report (PDF) – redactions will remove customer-identifying PII, exact external IP addresses tied to customers, and non-actionable screenshots that include customer data.
   - Remediation status CSV that maps finding IDs to remediation owner, current status (Open/In Progress/Fixed), and planned ETA.

2) Items we will keep internal / not include:
   - Internal detection playbooks and raw logs that contain customer identifiers.
   - Exact exploit scripts and reproduction steps that could be weaponized without a controlled release.

3) Redaction rules (attached): redaction_instructions.docx — please review the list; we will apply conservative redactions and add a redaction log page in the PDF noting what was removed.

4) Scope confirmation: the assessment covers external web tier and customer-facing REST APIs (OAuth-protected endpoints were included where we had test accounts). Internal-only services were out of scope.

5) Timeline & blockers:
   - We can produce the redacted PDF and the remediation CSV by 2027-04-12 18:00 PDT provided there are no additional legal constraints.
   - If Greenleaf requires unredacted artifacts (for in-house forensics), we need a signed NDA addendum and a documented access plan.

I’ve attached the redaction guidance and an export of current remediation items (remediation_state_Q2_2027.csv). If you want a brief call to go over the redaction decisions, I’m available Wed 4/7 10–11am PDT.

Laura Bennett
Head of Security | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
